nodes.name: IrOx Precipitation (Washed)
nodes.procedure: 299 mg of IrCl3 hydrate (1 mmol) and 591 mg of Li2CO3 (8 mmol) were dissolved in 10 mL of deionized water and stirred for 16 h at 25°C. A further 10 mL of deionized water was added, followed by heating to reflux for 3 h. The mixture was allowed to cool to room temperature. The formed precipitate was recovered by filtration and washed with 1 L of cold water and 1 L of hot water. The solid was dried in an open vessel at 25°C for 16 h.

nodes.name: Li-IrOx Synthesis (Unwashed + Annealing)
nodes.procedure: 299 mg of IrCl3 hydrate (1 mmol) and 591 mg of Li2CO3 (8 mmol) were dissolved in 10 mL of deionized water and stirred for 16 h at 25°C. A further 10 mL of deionized water was added, followed by heating to reflux for 3 h. After cooling to room temperature, the precipitate was recovered by filtration without any washing step, dried in an open vessel (25°C, 16 h), and annealed in static air (500°C, 10°C/min, 3 h). Excess Li2CO3 and Cl contamination were removed by washing with 1 L of hot and 1 L of cold deionized water. Finally, the material was dried in an open vessel at 25°C for 16 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fresh IrOx shows broad amorphous features at 35° and residual Li2CO3 diffraction; in situ heating shows r-IrO2 formation >425°C; Li-IrOx (heated with Li2CO3) shows exclusive nanocrystalline phase matching β-Li2IrO3 [ICSD-246025] with ~11 nm crystallites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD, Figure 1a) of the freshly prepared material shows broad features at 35°, typical of amorphous IrOx and low-intensity diffraction of residual Li2CO3 [ICSD-16713]. In situ diffraction during heat treatments shows rutile IrO2 [ICSD-56009] forms >425°C ... The sample with excess Li2CO3 crystallizes exclusively into a different phase (Li-IrOx) with a crystallite size of ~11 nm; a small residual broad feature is consistent with some remaining amorphous material.

nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy (TEM) shows that IrO_x appears, as expected, amorphous ... while Li-IrO_x is polycrystalline with nanocrystalline domains (Figure 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: r-IrO2 shows Ir 4f component at 61.8 eV consistent with crystalline rutile IrO2; IrOx and Li-IrOx show main component at 62.3 eV indicating highly hydrated/hydroxylated surfaces with Ir oxidation states below Ir(IV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS spectra of the Ir 4f levels (Figure 1c) were fitted ... A component (61.8 eV) consistent with crystalline rutile IrO2 was observed for the synthesized r-IrO2. An additional component (62.3 eV) appears ... this is the main component for the Li-IrOx material

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge NEXAFS shows r-IrO2 with strong A*/B* resonances at 530/533 eV for O2- species; IrOx and Li-IrOx show decreased A* intensity, splitting at 529 eV, and shifted C* resonances indicating longer Ir-O bonds and electrophilic oxyl species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surface oxygen species were investigated by O K-edge NEXAFS (Figure 1d) ... The r-IrO2 spectrum presents strong resonances at 530 and 533 eV ... A significant decrease in the A* intensity for IrOx indicates lower degree of hybridization ... Li-IrOx has a less intense A* resonance ... shifts to lower energy (~529 eV)

Table 1. EXAFS Model Fitting Parameters for Fresh r-IrO2, IrOx, Li-IrOx ... r-IrO2: Ir-O 1.97(2)Å 6.1(1.6), Ir-Ir1 3.14(2)Å 3.0(1.5), Ir-Ir2 3.55(1)Å 6.8(1.2); IrOx: Ir-O 2.013(4)Å 5.9(4); Li-IrOx: Ir-O 2.000(6)Å 6.3(5), Ir-Ir1 3.09(2)Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge XANES shows similar white line positions ~11,219.8-11,220.0 eV for r-IrO2, IrOx, and Li-IrOx indicating mixed Ir(IV)/Ir(III) valence; reduced white line height for disordered IrOx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a shows that r-IrO2, IrOx, and Li-IrOx have similar WL positions (11,219.8–11,220.0 eV) ... Comparison of Ir0, IrCl3, and IrO2 suggests a mixed valence Ir(IV)/Ir(III) species in the disordered IrOx material supported qualitatively by the reduced WL height.
